paragraphs.title: The Spirit Poured Out on All

answers: All flesh
Only the old men
Only the kings
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh.”
easy.q: Upon whom will God pour out His spirit?

answers: Build temples
Prophesy
Go to war
easy.explanation: The passage says, “your sons and your daughters shall prophesy.”
easy.q: What will the sons and daughters do?

answers: The young men
The servants
The old men
easy.explanation: The verse states, “your old men shall dream dreams.”

answers: Only the distinction between young and old
Distinctions of age, sex, and social status
The distinction between city and country dwellers
medium.explanation: The passage includes sons and daughters, old men and young men, servants and handmaids.
medium.q: What distinction among people is removed in the description of the Spirit being poured out?

answers: Speak or declare inspired messages
Sleep for a long time
Work the land
medium.explanation: The passage describes people receiving prophetic experiences, dreams, and visions.
medium.q: What does “prophesy” mean in this passage?

answers: The Spirit will bring prophecy, dreams, and visions
The Spirit will bring darkness and fire
The Spirit will cause a new city to be built
medium.explanation: After the promise of the Spirit, the passage mentions prophecy, dreams, and visions.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the Spirit being poured out and the experiences described?

answers: The spiritual experience is intended for many different groups
Only certain families will receive the Spirit
Young people are more important than old people
challenge.explanation: The passage lists people of different ages, sexes, and social statuses to show the breadth of the promise.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from mentioning sons, daughters, old men, young men, servants, and handmaids?

answers: Old men—dreams
Young men—prophecy only
Servants—darkness
challenge.explanation: The KJV says, “your old men shall dream dreams.”
challenge.q: Which pairing of a group and its experience appears in the passage?

answers: The Spirit will be given without limit to only one group
The Spirit will be given to people from all the groups mentioned
The Spirit will be given only to those who see visions
challenge.explanation: The following verses include people of different ages, sexes, and social statuses, including servants and handmaids.
challenge.q: What does “upon all flesh” mean in light of the following verses?

paragraphs.title: Signs Before the Day of the Lord

answers: Only in Jerusalem
In the heavens and on the earth
Only in the sea
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth.”

answers: Blood, fire, and pillars of smoke
Water, snow, and wind
Gold, silver, and stones
easy.explanation: The verse names “blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke.”
easy.q: Which things are listed among the wonders on earth?

answers: It will disappear from the heavens
It will be turned into blood
It will be turned into darkness
easy.explanation: The passage says, “The sun shall be turned into darkness.”
easy.q: What will happen to the sun?

answers: After the Day of the Lord
Before the coming of the Day of the Lord
Only after the remnant appears
medium.explanation: The sun and moon will be changed “before the great and the terrible day of the LORD come.”
medium.q: When will the wonders described in the passage appear?

answers: Columns of smoke rising upward
Heavy drops of rain
Rays of light from the moon
medium.explanation: The phrase describes tall columns or billowing streams of smoke.

answers: The sun will become dark and the moon will become blood
The sun will burn and the moon will disappear
The sun will become blood and the moon will become fire
medium.explanation: The KJV says, “The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood.”
medium.q: What change is described in both the sun and the moon?

answers: They are signs before the Day of the Lord
They describe the lives of servants
They describe the place of deliverance
challenge.explanation: The wonders are described before the coming of the Day of the Lord, so they serve as signs preceding it.
challenge.q: What is the function of the wonders according to the order of the passage?

answers: From the heavens and earth to the sun and moon
From Jerusalem to servants
From dreams to young men
challenge.explanation: The passage first mentions the heavens and earth, then specifically describes the sun and moon.
challenge.q: What transition occurs in the description of the wonders?

answers: A description of unusual and fearful signs
A description of an ordinary bright day
A description of a peaceful protected place
challenge.explanation: The changed sun and moon, together with blood, fire, and smoke, create a solemn and alarming picture.
challenge.q: What effect is created by combining darkness in the sun with blood in the moon?

paragraphs.title: Refuge on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem

answers: Whoever calls on the name of the LORD
Only those who live outside Jerusalem
Only the old men
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered.”

answers: Mount Zion and Jerusalem
The heavens and the earth
The sea and the wilderness
easy.explanation: The verse says, “in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance.”
easy.q: Which places will be places of deliverance?

answers: Those whom the LORD shall call
All nations without exception
Only those who saw the sun
easy.explanation: The passage refers to “the remnant whom the LORD shall call.”
easy.q: Who will remain among the remnant?

answers: Calling on the LORD leads to being delivered
Calling on the LORD causes darkness
Calling on the LORD prevents entrance into Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The verse directly states that whoever calls on the name of the LORD shall be delivered.
medium.q: What is the connection between calling on the name of the LORD and deliverance?

answers: Rescue and safety
A prophetic dream
A pillar of smoke
medium.explanation: In this context, deliverance means being rescued or spared.
medium.q: What does “deliverance” mean in this passage?

answers: As places where there will be deliverance
As places where there will only be smoke
As places where people will see dreams
medium.explanation: The KJV says that deliverance shall be found in Mount Zion and Jerusalem.
medium.q: How are Mount Zion and Jerusalem described?

answers: Deliverance is connected both with calling on the LORD and with those whom He calls
Deliverance is intended only for servants and handmaids
Deliverance depends on seeing the moon
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions both whoever calls on the LORD and the remnant whom the LORD shall call.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the connection between “whosoever shall call” and “the remnant”?

answers: Calling on the LORD, deliverance, refuge, and the remnant
Dreams, smoke, war, and Jerusalem
Darkness, prophecy, servants, and the sun
challenge.explanation: The verse moves from calling on the LORD to deliverance, then mentions Mount Zion, Jerusalem, and the remnant.
challenge.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in the verse?

answers: It is connected both with specific places and with people whom the LORD calls
It takes place only in the heavens
It is given only to those who dream dreams
challenge.explanation: The verse names Mount Zion and Jerusalem as places of deliverance and also refers to the remnant whom the LORD calls.
challenge.q: What is distinctive about the description of deliverance?
